title: The Ravenswood Kitchen Where Wallace Abbott Made His Own Granules
conflicts: Where production began: Abbott's history book says the kitchen of his small apartment (the Gale company history agrees), while Abbott's timelines and abbott.com say the rear of, or at, the People's Drug Store; the couple lived in the drugstore's frame house, so the story gives the kitchen and notes the drugstore version. The book names the firm the Abbott Alkaloidal Company in 1891 in one timeline and 1894 elsewhere; the story uses only the 1900 incorporation (confirmed by Gale). Sales figures ($2,000 in 1888, $8,000 in 1890) exist only in Abbott's own sources and are attributed as the company's count; Gale's $200,000 by 1905 is not used.
notes: The main source is Abbott's own 2013 history book, read through the text its online flipbook loads; it is celebratory and is attributed as the company's account. Independent support is thin (Gale's International Directory of Company Histories via Encyclopedia.com, plus Wikipedia once). The story ends with the decline of alkaloidal products from 1912 and the 1914 switch to synthetics. The repeat screen flagged the Beckman edition as same-founder but let it through; they are unrelated.
